title: Underwater glue breakthrough boosts repair efficiency and cuts carbon #shorts #glue #repairing
description: Japanese scientists have developed the strongest underwater adhesive by analyzing barnacle proteins, known for their natural ability to stick to rocks for millions of years. Using AI to study 24,000 adhesive proteins from sea creatures like mussels and barnacles, they engineered a novel material that is ten times stronger than existing glues. A single drop of this glue can hold the weight of a motorcycle engine, demonstrating unprecedented strength. The innovation extends beyond super adhesive properties—its real impact lies in environmental sustainability. The glue can seal underwater damage, such as a two-centimeter hole in a pipe under high pressure, enabling efficient underwater repairs without the need for extensive steel infrastructure or heavy equipment. This technology has the potential to reduce carbon emissions significantly by minimizing large-scale replacements and maintenance operations in marine settings. #underwaterglue #AIadhesive #barnacleinspired #carbonreduction #marineinnovation #sustainablematerials #biomimicry #underwaterrepair #environmentaltech #japanesescience #AIinnovation #carboncutting #adhesivetechnology #marineengineering #biotech
